Verify a set of 4 essential frequencies.

Source: R/comp_util.R
is_valid_freq_set.Rd

is_valid_freq_set is a function that verifies that a set of 4 essential frequencies (hi, mi, fa, and cr) forms a valid set of frequencies (i.e., each value is a non-missing, non-negative numeric value).

Usage

is_valid_freq_set(hi, mi, fa, cr, allow_noninteger = TRUE)

Arguments

hi

The number of hits hi (or true positives).

mi

The number of misses mi (or false negatives).

fa

The number of false alarms fa (or false positives).

cr

The number of correct rejections cr (or true negatives).

allow_noninteger

Boolean value for allowing non-integer (i.e., exact, non-rounded) frequencies. Default: allow_noninteger = TRUE.

Value

A Boolean value: TRUE if the 4 frequencies form a valid set; otherwise FALSE.

Details

Importantly, the values of the frequencies are not checked for consistency with current probabilities or population size parameters.

is_valid_freq_set is the frequency analog of is_valid_prob_set and uses is_freq-style criteria, but (by default) also accepts non-integer frequencies, as riskyr uses exact (i.e., non-rounded) frequencies internally. Setting allow_noninteger = FALSE additionally requires that all 4 frequencies are integers (e.g., for creating a population of individuals).

The function is vector-safe: When provided with vectors of frequencies, it returns a single Boolean value that is TRUE only if all elements are valid frequencies.

See also

is_freq verifies (integer) frequencies; is_valid_prob_set verifies sets of probabilities; comp_freq computes current frequency information; freq contains current frequency information.

Other verification functions: is_complement(), is_extreme_prob_set(), is_freq(), is_integer(), is_matrix(), is_perc(), is_prob(), is_suff_prob_set(), is_valid_prob_pair(), is_valid_prob_set(), is_valid_prob_triple()

Examples

is_valid_freq_set(1, 2, 3, 4)    # => TRUE
#> [1] TRUE
is_valid_freq_set(10.5, 2, 3, 4) # => TRUE (non-integer allowed by default)
#> [1] TRUE
is_valid_freq_set(10.5, 2, 3, 4, allow_noninteger = FALSE)  # => FALSE
#> [1] FALSE
is_valid_freq_set(1, 2, 3, NA)   # => FALSE (due to NA)
#> [1] FALSE
is_valid_freq_set(1, 2, 3, -4)   # => FALSE (due to negative value)
#> [1] FALSE
